what: Toast sells an all-in-one system for restaurants: point-of-sale terminals, payment processing, online ordering, payroll and lending. The hardware is sold near cost; payments and software are the business.
customers: Restaurants of all sizes in the United States, from single locations to chains, and increasingly outside the US.
money: software modules for ordering, payroll, marketing and inventory
moat: A system that runs the whole restaurant, from the kitchen display to payroll, which makes switching a disruption to daily operations rather than a vendor change.
risks: Gross margin of 26% is low because payment processing costs pass through
Restaurant closures reduce locations and therefore revenue
Competition for restaurant point-of-sale is intense
opportunities: Revenue grew about 24% last year and about 31% a year over three years
Return on invested capital of 13% with cash of $1.2 billion and almost no debt
Each new software module raises revenue per location without new customers
watch: Net location additions and annual recurring revenue per location.
